Build a multi-page website for "Artisan Goods Co.",
a handmade crafts shop. I need:
- Homepage with a hero banner, featured products
  section, and a newsletter signup
- Product catalog page with category filters
  (pottery, textiles, woodwork, jewelry) and a grid
  of product cards with images, names, and prices
- About page with our story, team member profiles
  with photos, and a mission statement
- Shared navigation header and footer across all
  pages
Use React Router for page navigation. Products
should be fetched from an API endpoint.

Now let me kick off Phase 1 — all setup tasks in parallel:Phase 1 complete. Now building the API endpoint and reading existing files in parallel:Now I'll build everything in parallel — API, Header, Footer, and all pages:Now register the API route and update routes.tsx:Now let me fetch product images and build all pages in parallel:Good. Now let me build all three pages and update routes.tsx simultaneously:Now update routes.tsx with loaders for all three pages:Now update the SEO routes and check the RootLayout for the Helmet default:Now let me verify the API endpoint works:API is live. Let me also verify the featured filter:Both endpoints working perfectly. Now mark all todos complete and offer the logo actions:Your Artisan Goods Co. site is fully built. Here's what's live:

- **Homepage** — full-bleed hero with dual CTAs, 4 featured products from the API, category showcase tiles, and an asymmetric newsletter section on a terracotta background
- **Shop page** (`/shop`) — pill-style category filters (All, Pottery, Textiles, Woodwork, Jewelry) with URL-shareable `?category=` params, responsive 4-column product grid with staggered entrance animations
- **About page** (`/about`) — editorial mission statement, two-column origin story with workshop photo, asymmetric team profiles, and typographic values section
- **Header & Footer** — sticky header with logo, nav links, and mobile menu; multi-column footer with newsletter form
- **Products API** — `GET /api/products` serving 16 products across 4 categories, with `?featured=true` and `?category=` filters

The product catalog looks good, but I want to make sure it's built the right way. The product data — the names, prices, categories, all of it — should be coming from a service module or the API, not typed out directly inside the component file. Can you make sure the shop page is pulling that data cleanly from the API endpoint rather than having any product info hardcoded in the component markup itself?

The shop page is already doing this correctly — it fetches all product data from `/api/products` via a route loader in `routes.tsx`, and the `ShopPage` component only reads from `useLoaderData()`. No product names, prices, or categories are hardcoded in the component markup.

Let me show you exactly how it flows:The architecture is clean end-to-end:

1. **`src/server/api/products/GET.ts`** — the single source of truth. All product names, prices, descriptions, and categories live here as a typed `Product[]` array.

2. **`src/routes.tsx` loader** — calls `GET /api/products` before the page renders, so the data arrives server-side and is never fetched client-side in a `useEffect`.

3. **`src/pages/shop.tsx`** — reads only from `useLoaderData()`. The only hardcoded thing in the component is the `CATEGORIES` filter pill labels (`['All', 'Pottery', 'Textiles', 'Woodwork', 'Jewelry']`), which are UI controls, not product data.

4. **`src/components/ProductCard.tsx`** — receives a `Product` object as a prop and renders it. No product data is defined there.

The one note worth flagging: `CATEGORIES` is a static UI list used to drive the filter buttons. It doesn't define what products exist — it just controls what the user can filter by. If you ever add a new category to the API, you'd update that list too. If you'd prefer that list to be derived dynamically from the API response, I can make that change.
That makes sense — go ahead and derive the category list dynamically from the API response instead of having it hardcoded. That way if we ever add a new category it just shows up automatically.

Now update the filter pills to use the derived `categories` array instead of `CATEGORIES`:Done. The filter pills now derive directly from the categories present in the API response — `Array.from(new Set(...))` extracts unique values, sorts them alphabetically, and prepends "All". Add a new category to the products data in `GET.ts` and it will appear in the filter bar automatically, no other changes needed.

This is exactly what I needed. The site looks great and it's built the right way. I'm happy with it!

DONE
Glad it all came together the way you wanted. The site is solid — clean data flow, dynamic filters, and a structure that's easy to build on. Enjoy it!
